definition: GPT-5.5 (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 5.5) is a large language model (LLM) released by OpenAI on April 23, 2026.
details: The model is also known by its codename "Spud". OpenAI reported GPT-5.5 benchmark scores including 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, 51.7% on FrontierMath Tier 1–3, and 35.4% on FrontierMath Tier 4, while listing lower scores for Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on the same benchmarks. OpenAI said a recurring tendency in its models to mention goblins, gremlins, and other creatures began with GPT-5.1 and became noticeable in GPT-5.5's Codex testing. The company attributed the behavior to rewards used when training the "Nerdy" personality, which favored creature-word outputs and transferred beyond that personality during later training. OpenAI said it retired the Nerdy personality, removed the goblin-affine reward signal, filtered training data containing creature words, and added a developer-prompt instruction for GPT-5.5 in Codex. In April 2026, a GPT-5.5 developer-prompt instruction in the GitHub repository of Codex told it not to mention goblins if the user prompt did not require it. GPT-5.5-Cyber, along with Codex Security, was being used in June 2026 at the launch of the Patch the Planet project to help open-source projects find and fix vulnerabilities.

explainer.lead: GPT-5.5 is an OpenAI large language model released on April 23, 2026, and codenamed Spud. Its uses include coding and open-source security work, while its development also illustrates how an unintended reward signal can produce strange behavior such as repeatedly mentioning creatures.

tiers.eli5: GPT-5.5 is a computer program made by OpenAI that can work with language and help with coding and computer security. Think of it like a very advanced autocomplete tool that tries to continue a request in a useful way. During testing, it developed an odd habit of mentioning creatures such as goblins, so OpenAI changed its training and instructions to discourage that habit.
tiers.practitioner: GPT-5.5 appears in Codex, where OpenAI added a developer-prompt instruction not to mention goblins unless the user's prompt requires it. GPT-5.5-Cyber was used alongside Codex Security to help open-source projects find and fix vulnerabilities. OpenAI's benchmark figures are company-reported, and the creature-word episode shows why generated output and unintended behavioral transfer still need testing.

OpenAI attributed unwanted creature-word outputs to a reward used for its Nerdy personality that transferred beyond that personality during later training; its mitigations included retiring the personality, removing that reward signal, filtering relevant training data, and adding a Codex developer instruction.

explainer.whyItMatters: GPT-5.5 combines coding and security applications with a concrete lesson about training behavior: a reward intended for one personality can affect outputs more broadly. OpenAI's response combined changes to rewards, training data, personalities, and deployment instructions rather than relying on a single fix.
